findings.snippet: result = await agent.run(extra_instructions or 'Please generate the object.')
findings.explanation: A model is invoked but there is no nearby moderation, schema validation, or output filtering. Raw model output can contain injected instructions, unsafe content, or malformed data that downstream code trusts.
findings.remediation: Validate the model's output before using it: enforce a schema (e.g. Pydantic), run a moderation/safety check, and constrain it to an allowlist of expected actions.

findings.title: User input concatenated directly into a prompt
findings.explanation: A prompt is built by interpolating a variable into a template. If that variable contains untrusted user input, an attacker can override your instructions (prompt injection).
findings.remediation: Keep the system instruction in a separate message from user content. Pass user text as its own 'user' role message rather than splicing it into the system prompt, and validate/escape it first.

findings.title: Generic bearer/secret assignment hardcoded in source
findings.explanation: A credential appears to be committed directly in the code. Anyone with repo access (or a leaked clone) can use it, and it stays in git history even after removal.
findings.remediation: Move the secret to an environment variable or a secret manager, rotate the exposed key immediately, and purge it from git history (git filter-repo / BFG).

findings.title: Possible sensitive data written to logs
findings.explanation: A logging statement references what looks like personal data or raw model input/output. Logs are often shipped to third parties and retained long-term, so this can leak PII and violate Law 25 / GDPR.
findings.remediation: Redact or hash sensitive fields before logging. Log identifiers and metadata, never raw user content, credentials, or full prompts/responses.
